description: Perceptual rubric for the screenshot-and-critique loop. Unlike the deterministic linter (which scores the DATA MODEL — coordinates, groups), this scores the RENDERED PIXELS the way a reader sees them. Each criterion maps to a corrective action in the same vocabulary the pipeline already uses.

criteria.question: Do any nodes, boxes, or labels overlap, touch, or sit on top of each other?
Is every label fully visible and comfortably readable — not clipped by its box, not truncated mid-word, not too small?
Are the connectors clean: orthogonal/consistent, few crossings, arrowheads clear, and edge labels not colliding with the lines or other edges?
Are related elements visually grouped (by proximity or a clear enclosure/lane) and unrelated ones clearly separated, with no accidental cross-group closeness?
Is there one consistent reading direction appropriate to the idiom (top-down for hierarchy/flow, left-right for sequence/process, concentric for importance)?
Is the drawing well-fitted and balanced — no large empty regions, no crowded corners, sensible aspect ratio, centred in frame?
Can you trace the main path (e.g. start → end, root → leaves) unambiguously without losing the thread?

pass: grade <= C and no criterion below 0.4
